title: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults
population: Healthy adults: novice, intermediate and advanced trainees.
key_findings: For hypertrophy it recommends loads from 1 to 12RM in a periodized fashion with emphasis on 6 to 12RM, rests of 1 to 2 minutes, moderate velocity, and higher-volume multiple-set programmes.

For strength in intermediate and advanced trainees it recommends 1 to 12RM periodized with eventual emphasis on 1 to 6RM and rests of 3 to 5 minutes; load rises 2 to 10% once one or two repetitions beyond the target are achieved.

Recommended frequency rises with experience: 2 to 3 days a week for novices, 3 to 4 for intermediates and 4 to 5 for advanced; it asks that recommendations be applied in context of goals, capacity and training status.
methods: Position stand of the American College of Sports Medicine: consensus recommendations from a review of the literature.
limitations: Published in 2009, before most of the meta-analyses on rest intervals, volume and failure in this library; consensus recommendations rather than a quantitative synthesis.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
